haiku-low.q1: They see the generic reply: 'If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link' (HTTP 200). Nothing is sent.
haiku-low.q2: Its count of the last hour's rows is 3 or more, so it rolls back. They get the generic reply only. No token is created and no email is sent.
haiku-low.q3: A link works for 30 minutes. A newer link request or a successful reset consumes it sooner.
haiku-low.q4: It stays usable: unconsumed and unexpired, since a rejected password writes nothing. The user can retry until it expires.
haiku-low.q5: None. All sessions are deleted, including the resetting device. The user is redirected to login, not logged in automatically, and signs in with the new password.
haiku-low.q6: The worker retries 3 times with backoff, then logs and drops the job. The user is not told, sees nothing, and must request again.
haiku-low.q7: The raw token is put in the queued 'reset' job. The worker builds APP_URL/reset?token=raw from it and sends the email. The raw token exists only there and in the link.
haiku-low.q8: It hashes the token with SHA-256 and looks up the row by token_hash. It checks consumed_at is null and expires_at is in the future. If so, it shows the form; otherwise the expired page.
haiku-low.q9: In the password_reset_tokens table, counted by created_at within the last hour. Old rows drop out of the count as the window moves. Rows are kept after expiry.
haiku-low.q10: Earlier unused tokens get consumed_at set to now, inside the request transaction, after the user row lock and count check, before the new row is inserted and committed.
haiku-low.q11: In one transaction: the token is consumed, the password hash is updated, and the user's sessions are deleted. The confirmation email is enqueued only after commit.
haiku-low.q12: The token UPDATE has WHERE consumed_at IS NULL AND expires_at > now RETURNING. Only one update matches; the other gets zero rows, rolls back, and sees the expired page.

sonnet.q1: They see the generic reply [G]: HTTP 200 'If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link.' Nothing is sent.
sonnet.q2: The count of tokens created in the last hour is already >= 3, so the transaction rolls back, no token is created and no email is sent. The user gets the same generic reply [G].
sonnet.q3: 30 minutes from creation (expires_at = created_at + 30 min). It can end sooner by being consumed: used via a successful password submit, or replaced when a newer link is requested.
sonnet.q4: Still usable. The server returns 400 with the reason and shows the form again; nothing is written and the link stays valid until it expires.
sonnet.q5: None. All the user's sessions are deleted, including the device that did the reset. The user is redirected (302) to the login page and must log in again with the new password; there is no auto-login.
sonnet.q6: The worker retries 3 times with backoff, then logs it and drops the job. The user is not told and has no link; they must request again, and each attempt uses quota. The design recommends alerting on dropped reset jobs.
sonnet.q7: The raw token is carried in the queued 'reset' job (with the email address). The worker builds the link APP_URL/reset?token=<raw> from it and sends the email.
sonnet.q8: It computes the SHA-256 of the token in the URL and looks up the row by that token_hash. The link is good if the row is unused (consumed_at null) and not expired; otherwise the expired page [E] is shown.
sonnet.q9: In the password_reset_tokens table itself: it counts the user's rows with created_at within the last hour. There is no separate counter; old rows drop out as their created_at passes beyond one hour (rows are kept after expiry).
sonnet.q10: Within the request transaction, after locking the user row and passing the count check, the earlier unused tokens are marked consumed (consumed_at = now), then the new row is inserted and committed.
sonnet.q11: In one transaction: the token is marked consumed, the user's password_hash is updated, and all the user's sessions are deleted. The 'password changed' email is enqueued after the commit.
sonnet.q12: The atomic UPDATE on the token row (SET consumed_at=now WHERE hash=h AND consumed_at IS NULL AND expires_at>now RETURNING user_id) is the real check. Only one submission gets a row back; the others get 0 rows, roll back, and see [E].
